heroText: Queenstown works best as a base in New Zealand when you anchor days around Lake Wakatipu, Skyline Queenstown and Queenstown Gardens. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Queenstown Airport (ZQN) handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.text: The first non-Māori to see Lake Wakatipu was European Nathanael Chalmers who was guided by Reko, the chief of the Tuturau, over the Waimea Plains and up the Mataura River in September 1853.

In 1860, Rees established a high country farm where Queenstown's town centre now stands, but the discovery of gold in the Arrow River in 1862 encouraged him to convert his wool shed into a hotel named the Queen's Arms, now known as Eichardt's.
By the start of 1864 Queenstown had multiple shops, several bars, a post office, a local newspaper, both an Anglican and Catholic church, and a timber yard.

history.label: 1860s
history.text: The tribe of Kāti Māmoe occupied a settlement called Te Kirikiri Pa where the Queenstown Gardens are today, but by the time European migrants arrived in the 1860s this settlement was no longer being used.
